extracted.intended_audience: USPTO staff, General Counsel, patent practitioners, attorneys serving subpoenas, and foreign governments submitting mask-work proclamation requests
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedures and standards governing Privacy Act disclosures, exemptions, fees, penalties, service of process, employee testimony and production of documents, indemnification and tort claims, and procedures for foreign requests for Presidential proclamations for mask works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure to persons other than the individual (§102.30(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may disclose a record pertaining to an individual to a person other than the individual only in enumerated instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated instances include: (1) upon written request by the individual (including authorization under §102.25(f)); (2) with the prior written consent of the individual; (3) to a parent or legal guardian under 5 U.S.C. 552a(h); (4) when required by the Act and not covered explicitly by 5 U.S.C. 552a(b); and (5) when permitted under 5 U.S.C. 552a(b)(1)–(12) which includes specific subcategories (i) agency officers/employees with need-to-know, (ii) disclosures required under 5 U.S.C. 552, (iii) routine use as defined, (iv) Bureau of the Census, (v) statistical research recipients with assurances, (vi) NARA, (vii) other agencies/instrumentalities for law enforcement with written request specifying portion and activity, (viii) compelling circumstances affecting health/safety with notice to last known address, (ix) either House of Congress/committees, (x) Comptroller General, (xi) pursuant to court order, (xii) to consumer reporting agency under 31 U.S.C. 3711(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations referencing §102.30(a)(4) (statutory obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies the specific statutory provisions that constitute 'required by the Act' disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (1) 5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(4) requiring dissemination of a corrected/amended record or notation of a disagreement statement in certain circumstances; (2) 5 U.S.C. 552a(d) requiring disclosure of records to the individual upon request; (3) 5 U.S.C. 552a(g) authorizing civil action by an individual and requiring disclosure by USPTO to the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting and notification of disclosures (§102.30(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy Officer must account for each disclosure of a record contained in a system of records and make such accounting available to any individual upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting is made in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(1) and (2). Except disclosures under 5 U.S.C. 552a(b)(7), the accounting is available to the affected individual on request per §102.24. Privacy Officer shall make reasonable efforts to notify individuals when records are disclosed under compulsory legal process, promptly upon being informed such process is public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for individuals under this part (§102.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only fees charged to or collected from an individual under this part are for duplication of records at the individual's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fees shall be charged for: search and retrieval of records; review of records; copying at USPTO initiative without a request; transportation of records and personnel; and first-class postage. USPTO policy is to provide one copy of each corrected/amended record to the individual without charge as evidence of the correction. As required by OPM regulations, USPTO will charge no fee for a single copy of certain personnel records covered by OPM's Government-wide notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for false pretenses (§102.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who knowingly and willfully obtain records under false pretenses are subject to criminal penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 5 U.S.C. 552a(i)(3), such persons shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and fined not more than $5,000. Additionally, false or fraudulent attempts to obtain records may be prosecuted under other criminal statutes (e.g., 18 U.S.C. 494, 495, 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: General exemptions—records from another agency (§102.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals may not have access to USPTO records that were provided by another agency which has determined those records are subject to a general exemption under 5 U.S.C. 552a(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exempt records are within an access request, USPTO will advise the individual of their existence and provide the name and address of the source agency; further inquiries must be directed to the source agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: General exemption justification—Investigative Records (§102.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO determines certain investigative records to be generally exempt from portions of the Privacy Act to protect law enforcement functions and confidential sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative Records—Contract and Grant Frauds and Employee Criminal Misconduct—COMMERCE/DEPT—12 are exempt pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 552a(j)(2) from most provisions of the Act except listed subsections. Justifications: ensure proper law enforcement functions, protect confidential sources, fulfill promises of confidentiality, prevent interference with proceedings, avoid disclosure of investigative techniques, avoid endangering personnel, avoid premature disclosure of criminal activity/evidence, and maintain integrity of law enforcement process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific exemptions—national defense/foreign policy materials (k)(1) (§102.34(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Some USPTO systems contain material subject to exemption at 5 U.S.C. 552a(k)(1) relating to national defense and foreign policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems within this exemption are listed (COMMERCE/PAT-TM-6, -7, -8, -9). USPTO claims exemption of such materials wherever they appear; such materials are exempt from select subsections (e.g., 5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(3), (d), (e)(1), (e)(4)(G),(H),(I), and (f)) to protect materials required by Executive order to be kept secret in interest of national defense/foreign policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific exemptions—k(2) & k(5) (investigative/litigation/attorney records) (§102.34(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain systems are exempt under 5 U.S.C. 552a(k)(2) and (k)(5) for reasons related to investigations, litigation, and sensitive personnel matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems listed (e.g., COMMERCE/DEPT-12, COMMERCE/DEPT-13, COMMERCE/DEPT-14, COMMERCE/PAT-TM-1, PAT-TM-2, PAT-TM-5) are exempted from specified subsections (c)(3), (d), (e)(1), (e)(4)(G),(H),(I), and (f). Reasons: prevent subjects from frustrating investigations; preserve law enforcement function; prevent disclosure of investigative techniques; protect confidentiality and sources; avoid endangering sources and personnel; maintain integrity; note: proviso imports due process protections and existence/general character of exempted information will be made known to the individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: No current claim of exemptions under k(3),(4),(6),(7) (§102.34(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO states it currently claims no exemption under 5 U.S.C. 552a(k)(3), (4), (6), and (7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of non-assertion—used to clarify scope of exemptions claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of this part to records noticed by other agencies (Appendix to Part 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains when provisions of this Part apply to records that are under other agencies' systems of records notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where systems apply only to USPTO, these regs apply; where they apply generally to components of the Department of Commerce, Department of Commerce regulations attach at point of denial for access or correction. Specific notes: OPM, DOL, EEOC, MSPB system notices may supersede or limit applicability of these provisions as described in the Appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address and manner for mail and service (§104.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies where mail and service of process must be directed for legal process matters under Part 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail: Office of the General Counsel, USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Hand service: Office of the General Counsel, 10B20, Madison Building East, 600 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA during business hours. Telephone: 571–272–7000 during business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rules by General Counsel (§104.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: General Counsel may waive or suspend rules of Part 104 in extraordinary situations when the interest of justice requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver may be sua sponte or on petition to the Director; General Counsel may impose conditions. Petitions must be accompanied by a petition fee of $130.00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to Federal Rules (§104.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Part 104 waives or limits any requirement under the Federal Rules of Civil or Criminal Procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must be followed in addition to any applicable Federal Rules; Part 104 does not supplant Federal procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of service of process rules (§104.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart B sets procedures when a summons and complaint is served on the Office, Director, or an employee in official capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to ensure efficient administration of the Office and not to impede legal proceedings. Does not apply to subpoenas (see Subpart C) or to personal service on employees for matters not related to official business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of service procedures (§104.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: How summons and complaints to the Office, Director, or employees in official capacity should be served and handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must comply with §104.2. An employee served shall immediately notify and deliver the summons and complaint to the Office of the General Counsel, note date/hour/place and method of service. When legal proceeding seeks to hold an employee personally liable for actions in official business, employee must be served personally per Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(e). An employee sued personally may be represented by DOJ at its discretion. Office will accept service only for an employee in the employee's official capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and exceptions for employee testimony and document production (§104.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart governs testimony of employees as witnesses and production/disclosure of Office documents pursuant to a demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: does not apply where (1) employee testifies regarding facts/events unrelated to official business, or (2) former employee is an expert in a matter in which they did not participate personally while at the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for demands for testimony or production (§104.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and content requirements for demands, subpoenas, and associated affidavits or declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must immediately notify GC of any demand; employees may not give testimony or produce documents to non-USPTO persons regarding matters under demand without GC approval. GC may authorize certified copies subject to fees. Demands must be addressed to the General Counsel per §104.2. Subpoenas must be served per Federal Rules and a copy sent to GC. Every demand (except when US is a party) shall be accompanied by an affidavit or declaration under 28 U.S.C. 1746 or 35 U.S.C. 25(b) stating: title of legal proceeding, forum, requesting party's interest, reason for demand, showing that desired testimony/documents are not reasonably available elsewhere, if testimony requested the intended use and a general summary of desired testimony, and a showing that no document could be used in lieu of testimony. Failure of attorney to cooperate in good faith may be basis for noncompliance. Determination to comply or not is not a waiver of other noncompliance grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures if General Counsel determines noncompliance (§104.22(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps to take when GC determines not to comply with a demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GC will seek DOJ representation and attempt to have subpoena modified or quashed. If DOJ representation cannot be obtained, employee should appear, produce copy of these rules, and state GC advised not to provide requested testimony/production. If tribunal rules demand must be complied with, employee shall respectfully decline, citing United States ex rel. Touhy v. Ragen, 340 U.S. 462 (1951).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert or opinion testimony restrictions (§104.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits and procedures regarding employees giving expert or opinion testimony in legal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If GC authorizes testimony in proceedings not involving the US, testimony must be limited to facts within personal knowledge. Employees shall not provide expert testimony regarding Office information, subjects, or activities except on behalf of the United States or a party represented by DOJ. GC may authorize expert testimony in exceptional circumstances under §104.3 showing it will not be adverse to Office/US interests. If asked for unapproved expert testimony, the witness shall: (i) respectfully decline to answer on grounds testimony is forbidden by this subpart; (ii) request opportunity to consult with GC; (iii) explain that approval may be provided after consultation. If tribunal orders testimony without opportunity to consult GC, witness shall refuse citing Touhy. If employee unknowingly provides such testimony, they must inform GC as soon as possible and provide a written summary. In proceedings where the US is a party, employee may not testify as an expert for any party other than the US.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demands for records protected by confidentiality statutes (§104.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demands for production of records or testimony regarding information protected by confidentiality statutes must meet statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records or testimony protected by Patent Act (35 U.S.C. 122), Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. 552a), Trade Secrets Act (18 U.S.C. 1905), or any other confidentiality statute must satisfy those statutes' disclosure requirements and associated rules before production/testimony will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting employee indemnification (§104.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and documentary requirements for an employee to request indemnification for civil actions arising from activities within scope of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After being served, within five (5) calendar days deliver all process/pleadings or attested true copies to General Counsel with a detailed report of circumstances. An indemnification request to satisfy a verdict/judgment/award will be considered only if timely submission under paragraph (a) is satisfied. Requests must be submitted through supervisory chain with: (i) appropriate documentation (copies of verdict, judgment, appeal bond, award, or settlement proposal); (ii) employee's explanation of how acting within scope of employment; (iii) employee's statement whether they have insurance or other indemnification source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tort claims procedure and finality (§104.41–104.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative claims against the Office filed under the Federal Tort Claims Act and related regulations, and finality of settlement/denial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative claims shall be filed per FTCA (28 U.S.C. 2672) and DOJ regulations (28 CFR Part 14) with General Counsel per §104.2. Only decisions of the Director or the General Counsel regarding settlement or denial of any claim under this subpart are final for purposes of judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for mask work proceedings (§150.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms used in Part 150 for Presidential proclamations under 17 U.S.C. 902, including Director, foreign government, interim order, mask work, presidential proclamation, request, proceeding, and Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key definitional guidance: 'Mask work' defined as a series of related images representing predetermined 3D pattern of materials on semiconductor chip layers; 'foreign government' includes duly-constituted executives of foreign nations or empowered intergovernmental organizations; 'request' means a foreign government's request for Presidential proclamation issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of evaluation for section 902 proclamation (§150.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director may initiate evaluation independently or upon direction, and shall initiate evaluation upon receipt of a request from a foreign government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director actions: may initiate evaluation of propriety of recommending issuance, revision, suspension, or revocation of a section 902 proclamation; must initiate evaluation upon receipt of a foreign government's request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements for section 902 proclamation requests (§150.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign governments' requests must include specified documentation and meet formatting/language requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must include: (1) copy of foreign law/legal rulings providing protection for U.S. mask works; (2) copy of regulations/administrative orders implementing protection; (3) copy of laws/regulations establishing or regulating registration (if any); (4) any other relevant laws/regulations/orders; (5) all copies must be unedited, full-text, and if possible reproduced from the original document; (6) all material must be in original language and if not in English must be accompanied by a certified English translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process for section 902 proclamation requests (§150.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director's procedures for evaluating a section 902 request, including use of section 914 proceedings, soliciting public comments, and resolving objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim order under section 914 has not been issued, Director may initiate a 914 proceeding for additional info. If interim order has been issued, that information will be used. After receiving a request, a Federal Register notice will request relevant and material comments on adequacy/effectiveness of protection; comments should include detailed explanations of deficiencies and dates/nature of problems and must be submitted within 60 days of the notice. Director notifies Register of Copyrights and Judiciary Committees. If comments present reasons against a proclamation, Director will contact party for verification and the requesting foreign government to attempt resolution; if unresolved, a public hearing may be held. The comments, 902 request, 914 info, and hearing info will be evaluated; Director forwards information with evaluation and draft recommendation to Secretary, who forwards recommendation to President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and terms of proclamation recommendations (§150.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation for issuance of a proclamation may include terms and conditions regarding the proclamation's duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to the President can specify temporal terms/conditions for the proclamation's effective duration; Director/Secretary involvement per §150.4 evaluation and forwarding procedures.
